questions.title: Why does the RoPE rescaling factor λ vary across dimensions in LongRoPE?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.1, the paper mentions that the search discovers non‑uniform λ values for each RoPE dimension. I understand that lower‑frequency dimensions are more tolerant of interpolation, but why do we need to rescale each dimension separately instead of applying a single global factor? How does this dimension‑specific scaling preserve positional information more effectively than the linear scaling used in PI?

questions.title: How does the token position threshold ℛ affect attention distribution?
questions.question_body: Finding 2 suggests that the first ℛ tokens should be exempted from interpolation. What is the intuition behind keeping initial tokens unscaled? Does this have to do with the causal attention mask focusing more on earlier positions, or is it related to streaming LLM architectures? Could you provide a concrete example of how λ=1 for the first 128 tokens changes the rotary encoding compared to applying a global λ?

questions.title: What is the role of the monotonicity constraint λ_i ≤ λ_{i+1} in the evolutionary search?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 enforces that λ values increase monotonically with RoPE dimension, citing NTK theory. Could someone explain why higher frequency dimensions (smaller indices) should have smaller λ? What would happen if we violated this constraint—would we also see increased perplexity or just slower convergence?

questions.title: Can you walk through an example of a two‑step progressive extension from 4k to 2048k?
questions.question_body: The progressive strategy in Section 3.2 involves: (1) searching for 128k rescaling factors, fine‑tuning to 128k, (2) searching for 256k, fine‑tuning to 256k, and then (3) a second search on the 256k‑fine‑tuned model for 2048k. How exactly are the rescalers from step (1) reused in step (2)? Are they frozen or further mutated? Also, what is the rationale for splitting fine‑tuning into two short stages instead of a single longer run?

questions.title: Why does performance degrade on short context windows after an extreme extension?
questions.question_body: Section 3.3 mentions that after extending to 512× (2048k), positions within the original 4k become 'crowded,' hurting performance. Is this due purely to positional embedding compression, or does it also affect self‑attention sparsity? How effective is the recovery search at short lengths—does it simply re‑scale λ back towards 1 or is there more involved?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE compare theoretically with NTK and YaRN interpolation?
questions.question_body: "Finding 1" claims LongRoPE outperforms PI, NTK, and YaRN on perplexity for long windows without fine‑tuning. Given that NTK already uses dimension‑dependent scaling and YaRN groups dimensions into three regimes, what new non‑linearities or search strategies contribute most of LongRoPE’s advantage? Is it mainly the evolutionary search over a larger discrete space or the inclusion of token‑position non‑uniformity?

questions.title: What are the practical limits of scaling λ up to s×1.25 in the search space?
questions.question_body: When defining the search space, λ_i is allowed up to s×1.25 where s is the target extension ratio. Why choose 1.25 as a multiplier? Does going beyond this boundary lead to unstable training or loss of information? How sensitive is perplexity to small variations around this upper bound?

questions.title: Could LongRoPE be applied to other positional embeddings beyond RoPE?
questions.question_body: The paper focuses exclusively on rotary embeddings. Can the same idea—dimension‑wise and token‑wise rescaling searched by evolution—be adapted to sinusoidal positional encodings or learned absolute positions? Would we expect similar gains or are there theoretical reasons why rotary embeddings benefit more from non‑uniform interpolation?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE handle extremely long passages during inference in terms of memory and compute?

"LongRoPE-2048k" reports perplexities on documents up to 2 M tokens but doesn't detail runtime costs. Does using longer RoPE embeddings increase GPU memory usage proportionally? Are there any tricks (e.g., caching key/value pairs) required at inference time to keep compute tractable?
